a.text: I pray that the sick people in Faber Central Hospital get better!
I pray that Papà, Mamma, and my sister will always be safe, healthy, and happy!
I pray that the Lord will always be with us!
I pray that the spiritual light will always shine on Laterano!

steps.text: 'I thought the experiment was over, Lemuel.'
'Didn't you hear? The investigators came to school today to tell us our results. They even brought fruit tarts!'
'The two patient groups at Faber Central Hospital were discharged today... basically, their recovery had nothing to do with our praying the past two months.'
'The investigators told us not to be sad. It was all a social experiment by the Sixth Tribunal.'

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Another report from Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Over the past six months, they have established trade with seventeen nomadic cities, like a direswine that never rests.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: In the process, they have sown new seeds across all Siracusa.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: It sounds like you approve of Nuova Volsinii's interactions with other cities, but do not intend to endorse their promotion of the New Urban Management Act.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: You were the one who told me the youth need to be tested further, after you returned from Carnevale.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: I suppose I recall something to that effect.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: News from Terni. Unusual movement in Lupukarn.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: The Golden Empress has been actively issuing edicts, while her counterpart has not been seen in public for a long time... our neighbor seems eager to change. Desperate, even.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Not just Leithanien. There are more than enough new sprouts upon this land. The matters of the famiglie should not occupy any more of Siracusa's time.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Mm-hm.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: You seem ready to fall asleep.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: It's almost time for my siesta.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Do you like this fabric?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: I can have a suit made for you. I have just the tailor in mind.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Hah. I appreciate the offer, but there's no need.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Still prefer your cassock?

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: I am a priest, Sicilia.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: But there is no church in this city. It's been almost seventy years since you left Laterano, hasn't it?

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Sixty-eight. The Sankta sense of self is as persistent as our sweet tooth.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: But you've never thought about going back. You have no need to. The walls are still white, the people still happy. Nothing ever changes in Paradise.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Otherwise, you wouldn't have come with me to Siracusa.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: I'm not so sure...

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: My hand's been trembling every time I grip my patron firearm. Maybe my old house in the Holy City has sprung a leak.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: We're relics of a bygone age, Sicilia. You know how old people have hunches about certain things.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: *Yawn*—

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: You should take a nap on the sofa.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Maybe we can find another setting to talk, once the down payment for this fabric has been made.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Sorry, sorry.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Zzz...

steps.name: Panicked Apprentice
steps.text: Father? You didn't just fall asleep on your feet, did you? Father! Are you alright?!

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Urryyyyy—

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: What? Is that all?

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: Tila. Is the boss alright?

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: Why do you ask?

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: These are all documents that he reviewed. The only thing Legal changed was the formatting. He shouldn't need to spend so much time with them, should he?

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: I think Mr. Cliff is looking at that letter.

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: The letter from the frontier? What was the name on it again? Woodrow?

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: But there were only four words in it. 'Am well. Take care.' That's it.

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: I've heard a couple things about Davistown...

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: What are you getting at?

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: This ship will be approaching Max D.C. in twelve hours' time. How long have we been planning our entry into the capital market?

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: There're still a lot of problems to solve. Look at the people behind me. All our top ranks are waiting for the boss's orders!

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: But at a time like this, he's all tied up with his... his—I don't even know what to call him!

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: Mr. Cliff went to meet a certain Mr. Jackson before we set out.

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: Th-The Vice President?

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: Do you mean to say the boss has gotten the official nod to our cooperation with the companies in DC—

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: Don't get too excited.

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: No employee of Blacksteel Worldwide should doubt 'Clip' Cliff. Anything you don't think of, he will; anything you can't figure out, he will.

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: He was the one who put this team together, and he was the one who spread firearms beyond the walls of Laterano.

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: He was the one who expanded our business across the frontier, and beyond Columbia.

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: Mr. Cliff is a great leader, and a remarkable Sankta.

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: I agree completely, but... have you seen the look on his face? What could those four words have done to him?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Ladies and gentlemen—

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: What? Did the power go out?

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: Did some stupid merc knock something over? Or did Engineering cross the wrong wires?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Good news!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: The wildfire's finally extinguished.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: The bad news is that half the hillside has been burned away—

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woody? Are you okay? Are you hurt?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: *cough* *cough* I'm fine... it's nothing.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: He just came back from the woods to the west, where the worst of the fires were. He braved the flames to clear a control line.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: He might have forgotten his age...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Can't let the fire take it all, not when things are finally looking up in these parts—I'm fine, I really am...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: That's good to hear. I was worried.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Say, Woody, do you want to look at this?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: That's thick. Some kind of important document?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: It's from Blacksteel.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: You're not gonna open it, Woody?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: No, I don't think I want to.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: What if it's a whole stack of gold certificates? Would go a long way to filling the gap the fires left behind.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Well then, YOU open it.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Gladly.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Well, Mr. Cliff sure can write a letter. It's so long the end is touching the ground.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: What's the matter, Woody?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I... suddenly have a headache.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Is it the letter, or your wounds?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Were you waiting long?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Ezell!

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Happy Birthday, Cecelia!

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: This cake...

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: I, er, made it out of sweet potato.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: I couldn't find cream or confetti sugar, so I sprinkled some dried vegetables on top of it. I tried to find the ones that had better colors...

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Sorry, I did my best... 'slaves' don't have access to the nicest things. Galena helped out.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: It's lovely!

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Make a wish, Cecelia... well, I can guess what you'll wish for. Don't worry, I've been asking around. We'll find your father.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: But my wish today is—I want to blow out the candles with you.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: You've been helping me ever since I lost my mama, even quitting your job at the Notarial Hall and coming with me all the way to Kazdel.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: You've been by my side for so long.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I know you're in a lot of danger here, where my papa was born. It was you who taught me not to give up hope.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: That's why I want you to do this with me, the last thing at my birthday party.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Cecelia...

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Okay.
Ezell feels the warmth of Cecelia's hand in his own.

He sees the birthday cake made from sweet potatoes, and the girl with eyes full of excitement, and the big smile on her face. Before the flickering candlelight, both of them bow their heads and begin to pray.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: May the order of Laterano shine upon us♪

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Show us the path of life♪

steps.name: Cecelia & Ezell
steps.text: That we may ever live in joy♪
East of the east of La Unidad♪
Laterano, holy city of white♪

steps.name: Alert Nun
steps.text: Is that you, Aurela?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Such noise.

steps.name: Alert Nun
steps.text: We're due for hymns in ten minutes. The children are practicing.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I'm talking about you, Nueda.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: ...Is it done?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Buried in the backyard. You can breathe easy now.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Shouldn't you wash the blood first? The children could come at any time.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: What, are you afraid they might see me? Afraid they might hear their beloved Sister Nueda talk of killing people with that terrifying piece of metal?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Don't talk like that. We wouldn't be here if not for you... because you took up the gun, I am able to teach them hymns, and tuck them into bed.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Was it Singas soldiers, or True Bolívarians guerrillas this time?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Does it make a difference? A bunch of stinking parásitos who only know how to take from others.

spans.text: Does it make a difference? A bunch of stinking
who only know how to take from others.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Never imagined there were shitholes like this when I lived in Laterano.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I know... these sorts of things don't happen where you come from... in Laterano.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Your weapon, your dress, your habits... you still carry yourself as a Lateran.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: A Lateran? Pah.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Honestly, I still don't know why you follow the Lateran faith.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I grew up in Bolívar, with no one to rely on. All I've ever known are these parásitos.

spans.text: I grew up in Bolívar, with no one to rely on. All I've ever known are these

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I wanted to believe there was more to the land than ruined houses and barren fields, more than just war, death, and taxes. I wanted to believe there was a place full of food, flowers, and hope...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: And you wanted those chicos to believe it too.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: One person's faith is no faith at all. We all need to look out for each other, like you and I do...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I wouldn't say we're looking out for one another.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Shh... Aurela, you have protected this place as the holy light protects Laterano. You've let me imagine a Paradise bathed in holy light... even if I've never been there.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Which is for the better.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: If you really do believe in a Paradise bathed in holy light, it's definitely not Laterano you're looking for. Look elsewhere.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: We're about to abandon this abbey, after all.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Time to go in, Sister.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: The children are waiting for you to lead the last verse.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Aurela...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Why did you leave Laterano?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Because I sinned, that's why... idiota.
Nueda pushes the chapel door open.
East of the east of La Unidad♪
Laterano, holy city of white♪
There, the earth hides no bombs♪
There, the fields share wheat most bright♪
Abode of our Lord, font of parental love♪
He hears our prayers, He grants our wishes♪
All shall bask in His love♪
Even the legless, even the armless♪

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: ...This might be our last Vespers.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: For years, we've tried to keep a low profile in this lawless land, to avoid the attention of the Singas nobles and the thugs who call themselves guerrillas.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: But they followed the trail of some escaped convicts, and found our abbey. They're now looking at our farms and burdenbeasts.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Aurela has scouted the area. Tonight, she will lead us through a nearby canyon, and we will leave this place.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: We might go north into the plains, or south into the jungles. It will be a long trip, but we've been blessed with a good harvest. We will have enough food...

steps.name: Bolívarian Child
steps.text: Sister—

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Don't worry, Hugo.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Trust Aurela. Trust me. Trust yourself and those around you. And trust 'Laterano'...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Keep your voice steady. You remember the last verse, don't you?
East of the east of La Unidad♪
Laterano, holy city of white♪
The guns there shoot fireworks♪
The targets are all apples♪
Through the chapel windows, Nueda watches the sunset. The halos of the Sanktas in the procession continue to illuminate the room, and the choir sings.

She has sung these hymns countless times. It is said that they were first written down by the saints, on their long and difficult journeys, and passed down through the centuries, translated and arranged by Bolívarian scholars.
'Laterano' will protect them through briar and bramble, through the long, cold night.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: What the...?!
Perhaps the sun left too soon and forgot to leave some light. The halos and wings of the Sanktas in the choir suddenly shatter, and their light is extinguished.
Nueda is stunned.
Her esoteric knowledge is vast, thanks to the legacy of the K'uk'ulkan, but not a single word or symbol explains the scene before her eyes.
She is so stunned that she forgets to stop singing, murmuring the hymns by sheer instinct. Trembling voices echo through the chapel—
Abode of our Lord, font of parental love♪
He punishes evil and drives out injustice♪
All shall bask in His love♪
Whether they have scars or stones♪
When we pray sincere, He gives us bread♪
When we seek salvation, He sets us free♪

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Merda!

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Agenir, your halo—

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Diamine!

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: Wh-What's going on?

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: Calm down. We figured out what's going on. Somebody forgot to set the right parameters when testing a gun at the firing range. Accidentally overloaded the power grid.

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: Engineering's on it and the power should come back any minute now... although, something doesn't feel quite right.

steps.name: Blacksteel Administrator
steps.text: It's pitch black. Of course something doesn't feel right—

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: That's it! Where's Mr. Cliff's halo? It should be shining like a lamp—

steps.name: Tila
steps.text: Mr. Cliff?!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Woody?! I'll get a doctor!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woody... no...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Ezell... your halo... your wings... what...?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: I'm fallen...?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Why...?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: W-Was it my fault?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Ugh—Laterano...

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Seniora Lemuen!

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Saw you from across the street, but you didn't answer when I called your name...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I was about to—

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Oh, I forgot! It's your first day!

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Let's see. 'Your Eminence, Cardinal Lemuen', is that right?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It is giving me goosebumps.

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Hey, from submitting the application to becoming a cardinal's aide to finally getting the job, all it took was two years, right?

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Isn't that a new record for the Seventh Tribunal?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It took much longer than breaking the wheelchair speed-shooting record.

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Just a joke.

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Well, we all look up to you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: There are two hundred households up and down three streets waiting for you to deliver the cystymilk for their morning fruit tart and post-meal desserts...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Meanwhile, how often is a cardinal's presence really needed for diplomatic and national security business in Laterano?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Who's to say which one of us is more important to the city?

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Fair point. Guess I should get to work!

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: I'll leave your cystymilk at the door. Two servings, as usual?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Where's Seniora Lemuel working, anyway? One day I hear it's a logistics company in Lungmen, the next day I hear it's security for that pharma company called Rhodes Island...

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: I miss her. It's been a long time since I last saw her.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Who knows? Maybe she'll just show up tomorrow. And she wouldn't be happy if the fridge were empty.

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: You got that right.

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Hm, isn't this a bit of a detour if you're headed to the Seventh Tribunal?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Just visiting a friend I haven't seen in a long time.

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: I see... have a nice day, Cardinal Lemuen.

steps.name: Milkman
steps.text: Have an uneventful day. May the Law be with you and me.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Have a nice day.
Lemuen greets a few familiar faces on the way, then makes a turn at a corner, onto an utterly unremarkable street.
The clouds cast their shadows on the pristine paths. A breeze brings the sweet aroma in the air along with it. Soon, the surroundings grow quiet, as Lemuen approaches her destination.
Her life has undoubtedly changed. But her steps are light. She gladly welcomes these changes.
Lemuen has always been that way.
The Laterans have always been that way.
'Have an uneventful day. May the Law be with you and me.'
Lemuen utters those words.
At the end of the street is a massive building that nearly touches the clouds. The streamlined structure seems decidedly out of place amongst the low profile of church buildings around it.
It is no exaggeration to say that it virtually appeared out of nowhere, yet it also seems like it has always been there.
It welcomes Lemuen's arrival with open arms.
